fichas.title: Sustainability and design principles
fichas.summary: Sustainability is framed as development that meets current needs without endangering future generations’ ability to meet their own needs. The page presents regeneration, substitution, and adaptability as management rules, alongside design principles for resource circulation, recycling, reuse, and controlled demolition.
uses: Reduce resource use and environmental impacts
Support recycling, continued use, and reuse

fichas.title: Sustainable building
fichas.summary: Sustainable building considers economic, ecological, and social effects across the building life cycle, from design and construction through use, refurbishment, and demolition. Project-specific measures should account equally for social and cultural effects, while minimizing resource and energy use and harm to natural systems.
uses: Plan and assess buildings across their life cycle
Reduce consumption of natural resources, energy, and water
Support suitable residential environments and healthy living

fichas.title: Sustainable architecture and service life
fichas.summary: Architectural quality, design, and planning contribute decisively to sustainability. The page emphasizes relating construction cost to expected service duration and prioritizing a typologically flexible building structure, whose renewal cycle is longer than that of building services. Figure 4 compares building-envelope area with usable building area.
